bridges.name: Orientation-Closure Bridge (Topological Selection)

statement.informal: Orientation coherence conditions admissible knot-class selection but is not independently sufficient for closure stability.
statement.formal: -(i) conditions selection on T in the chain Delta -> R -> T -> A_adm -> delta_a

MODEL_D.name: Topological Selection Model
MODEL_D.description: Orientation is a selector/constraint on admissible closure topology, while stability arises from residue-conditioned topological admissibility (Principle 2.X).

hypotheses.H0: Orientation coherence has no independent effect on knot-class selection or admissible topology.
hypotheses.H1: Orientation coherence narrows the set of admissible knot-classes (T).

bridges.success_condition: Orientation coherence significantly narrows the distribution of observed knot-classes in admissible regimes.

failure_conditions.minimum: Knot-class distribution is identical regardless of orientation coherence.
failure_conditions.strong: Knot stability depends only on residue accumulation (R), with orientation providing no predictive shift in topological class.

statement.informal: Coherent orientation is induced by stabilized triadic closure of distinction-nodes.

MODEL_C_V2.name: Induced Alignment Model
MODEL_C_V2.description: Coherent orientation alignment emerges dynamically within persistent, stabilized triadic closures.

hypotheses.H0: Orientation coherence remains random regardless of triadic stability.
hypotheses.H1: Triadic stability induces orientation alignment (C_orient growth).

failure_conditions.minimum: Orientation coherence remains random under stable closures.
failure_conditions.strong: Orientation drift diverges regardless of triadic stability.

bridges.name: Orientation-Closure Bridge (Procedural Model)

statement.informal: Procedural orientating maintains the core invariants of the admissibility window.

MODEL_C.name: Independent Aspect Model
MODEL_C.description: Orientation (procedure) and closure (structural invariant) are decoupled signatures of a common underlying recursive residue field (K).

bridges.reason_for_rewrite: PD_CG_V2 justified procedure-level re-audit, but PD_CG_V2R did not support promotion of the _R-conditioned improvement route. The active governed baseline is now bare preserved distinction pending direct baseline-vs-qualifier testing.
bridges.governance_note: PD_CG_PATCH_003_SUBSCRIPT_BASELINE_RESET: use bare <≠> as baseline; treat subscripts as candidate conditioning qualifiers only; do not promote <≠>_R / <≠>_r without a new direct baseline comparison win.

bridges.name: Affect-Effect Quantitative Projection Bridge

statement.informal: The qualitative affect-effect relation may be projected into a bounded compatibility measure only after a declared representation map and overlap rule are supplied.
statement.formal: (A|E) --Pi_R--> P_R(A,E) = |<M_R(A)|M_R(E)>|^2; directional form P_R(E <- A) = |K_R(A -> E; B,O,M_R)|^2

MODEL_AE_OVERLAP.name: Reference-Relative Overlap Model
MODEL_AE_OVERLAP.description: Affect and Effect remain qualitative relational roles. M_R embeds admissible RT conditions into a declared quantitative representation space, Pi_R evaluates represented overlap, K_R preserves declared Affect-to-Effect directionality before squaring, and P_R is compatibility by default rather than probability.

MODEL_AE_DIRECTIONAL.name: Directional Affect-Effect Amplitude Model
MODEL_AE_DIRECTIONAL.description: K_R(A -> E; B,O,M_R) is a reference-boundary-orientation-relative amplitude carrier. It distinguishes the procedural role order A -> E from E -> A unless an explicit symmetry condition is declared.

hypotheses.H0: Reference-relative representation metadata does not affect projected affect-effect overlap values.
hypotheses.H1: Reference, boundary, orientation, and representation choices condition projected affect-effect overlap values.

bridges.success_condition: Projected overlap is bounded in [0,1] under normalized representation while preserving recoverable reference, boundary, orientation, representation, and directionality metadata.

failure_conditions.minimum: The projection is used without declared M_R, V_R, or overlap rule.
failure_conditions.strong: The bridge identifies raw Affect and Effect with quantum states or treats P_R(A,E) as probability without normalized exclusive alternatives.

open_obligations: Define whether M_R is linear, nonlinear, or domain-selected.
Specify whether Affect and Effect occupy the same representation space or dual spaces.
Validate or refine the provisional K_R(A -> E; B,O,M_R) directionality carrier under concrete representation choices.
Define probability normalization over mutually distinguishable candidate effects before probability language is permitted.

discharged_obligations.obligation: Define directional relational amplitude K_R(A -> E) or equivalent directionality carrier.

bridges.name: Typed-Zero Provenance

statement.informal: Typed zero conditions retain directional provenance only through a complete TZR carrier and may enter higher-order recoupling only through a declared typed-zero recoupling relation.

MODEL_TZR_PROVENANCE.name: Typed-Zero Provenance Carrier
MODEL_TZR_PROVENANCE.description: Directional zero states remain typed only if TZR preserves polarity, source trace, collapse context, admissibility context, and relation slot.

MODEL_TZR_RECOUPLING.name: Typed-Zero Recoupling Relation
MODEL_TZR_RECOUPLING.description: <g>_y is the scoped <*>_x family member governing recoupling between TZR(0_minus) and TZR(0_plus) under declared context y.

hypotheses.H0: Typed zero states collapse into undifferentiated zero under recoupling.
hypotheses.H1: Typed zero states retain directional provenance under a declared carrier and recoupling rule.

bridges.success_condition: A formal typed-zero provenance carrier, outer relation, and collapse condition are defined without asserting temporal priority or independent zero-object ontology.

failure_conditions.minimum: 0_minus and 0_plus are used in higher-order RT without declared provenance retention.
failure_conditions.strong: Typed zero is treated as an independent object or collapses into undifferentiated zero while still being used as typed evidence.

open_obligations: Validate that TZR carrier fields are sufficient for all uses of 0_minus and 0_plus in nested RT traces.
Audit existing <g>_y and <*>_x usages for compatibility with typed-zero recoupling.
Construct a PRIN_001 trace example showing lawful typed-zero recoupling without identity collapse.
Construct a counterexample showing collapse to 0_untyped when provenance fields are missing.

discharged_obligations.obligation: Define the structure preserving directional provenance in 0_minus and 0_plus.
Identify the member of the <*>_x family governing the outer recoupling relation.
Define collapse conditions under which typed zero becomes undifferentiated zero.

bridges.name: Cross-Domain Continuation Trace

statement.informal: Cross-domain continuation trace is provisionally formalized through an unresolved-continuation carrier and admissibility-preserving handoff rule that preserves declared trace invariants and orientation-reference continuity across projection boundaries.
statement.formal: H_adm(UC_i, tau_{i->j}) -> UC_j | bottom_C^{type} | bottom_C^{adm} | bottom_C^{trace}

MODEL_CROSS_DOMAIN_HANDOFF.name: Admissibility-Preserving Domain Handoff
MODEL_CROSS_DOMAIN_HANDOFF.description: An unresolved admissible meta-relation may preserve continuation trace across declared projection boundaries only if domain-transition types, trace invariants, and orientation-reference continuity are explicit.

MODEL_UNRESOLVED_CONTINUATION_TRACE.name: Unresolved Continuation Trace Carrier
MODEL_UNRESOLVED_CONTINUATION_TRACE.description: UC(C_i; D_i, R_i, O_i, B_i) carries a scoped continuation candidate, source domain, residue context, orientation reference, and projection boundary without implying time, observer persistence, consciousness, or identity survival.

hypotheses.H0: Continuation trace cannot be lawfully preserved across domain transitions without adding a new primitive.
hypotheses.H1: A typed admissibility-preserving handoff can preserve scoped continuation trace across domain transitions.

bridges.success_condition: A typed cross-domain handoff rule preserves declared trace invariants under projection change without promoting observer, time, consciousness, or identity-survival claims.

failure_conditions.minimum: Cross-domain continuation is asserted without declared domain-transition typing.
failure_conditions.strong: The bridge is used to claim subjective continuity, consciousness persistence, or trans-domain identity.

open_obligations: Construct a positive typed handoff example across two declared projection domains.
Construct a type-failure counterexample where no tau_{i->j} is declared.
Construct a trace-failure counterexample where residue or orientation-reference invariants are lost.
Audit existing typed-continuation-domain rules for compatibility with H_adm.
Define whether H_adm composes associatively across more than one projection boundary.

discharged_obligations.obligation: Define orientation-reference continuity under projection change.
